Implementation and rule wiring: - Rule source: src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts - JSDoc header explicitly links to this story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION` - `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE` - Exports an ESLint RuleModule named `rule` with: - `meta.type: "problem"` - `meta.docs.description: "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches"` - `meta.fixable: "code"` - `meta.messages.missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}."` - `meta.schema` defining an options object with `branchTypes` array (unique strings, no additional properties) - `create(context)`: - Calls `validateBranchTypes(context)` from `../utils/branch-annotation-helpers`. - If validateBranchTypes returns a listener (invalid config), it returns that directly, providing config error handling. - Otherwise, iterates the list of branch types and registers a handler per type: - Special-cases `SwitchCase`: skips branches where `node.test == null` (default case treated as non-significant). - Calls `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)` for each configured branch type.
- Branch helper utilities: src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts - `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES`: - Annotated with this story and REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA. - Value: ["IfStatement", "SwitchCase", "TryStatement", "CatchClause", "ForStatement", "ForOfStatement", "ForInStatement", "WhileStatement", "DoWhileStatement"]. - This set matches the story’s requirement to detect significant branches (if/else, try/catch, switch, loops). - `validateBranchTypes(context: Rule.RuleContext)`: - Annotated with `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - Reads `context.options[0]` and inspects `branchTypes`. - If `branchTypes` is an array: - Filters using `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.includes(...)` to find invalid types. - When invalid types exist, returns a RuleListener `{ Program: ProgramHandler }`. - `ProgramHandler` reports, for each invalid type, a message of the form: - `Value "" should be equal to one of the allowed values: IfStatement, SwitchCase, TryStatement, CatchClause, ForStatement, ForOfStatement, ForInStatement, WhileStatement, DoWhileStatement`. - This matches the story’s invalid configuration behavior and **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE**. - When there are no invalid types: - Returns the provided `branchTypes` array as-typed, or `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES` if no `branchTypes` option was provided. - `gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node)`: - Annotated with REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION. - Special handling for `SwitchCase`: - Looks at up to `PRE_COMMENT_OFFSET` (2) lines above `node.loc.start.line`. - Uses regex `/^\s*(\/\/|\/\*)/` to detect line or block comments. - Accumulates and joins comment lines into a single string. - For other nodes: - Uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and maps each comment node to its `.value`, then joins. - This associates inline or preceding comments with each branch, covering both line and block comments and handling switch-case layout nuances. - `reportMissingStory(context, node, { indent, insertPos, storyFixCountRef })`: - Annotated with REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING. - If `storyFixCountRef.count === 0`: - Reports `missingAnnotation` with data `{ missing: "@story" }` and fixer inserting: - `${indent}// @story .story.md\n` at `insertPos`. - Increments `storyFixCountRef.count`. - For subsequent missing @story on the same run: - Reports the error without fixer. - This provides auto-fix behavior for the first missing @story per run, as seen in tests. - `reportMissingReq(context, node, { indent, insertPos, missingStory })`: - Annotated with REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING. - If `missingStory` is false (story present but req missing): - Reports `missingAnnotation` with data `{ missing: "@req" }` and fixer inserting `${indent}// @req \n` at `insertPos`. - If `missingStory` is true: - Reports `missingAnnotation` with data `{ missing: "@req" }` without fixer. - Internal `getBranchAnnotationInfo(sourceCode, node)`: - Calls `gatherBranchCommentText` and determines: - `missingStory = !/@story\b/.test(text)`. - `missingReq = !/@req\b/.test(text)`. - Computes indentation from `sourceCode.lines[node.loc.start.line - 1]` and `insertPos` via `getIndexFromLoc`. - `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)`: - Annotated with REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING. - Uses `getBranchAnnotationInfo` to derive missingStory/missingReq, indent, insertPos. - Builds an `actions` array describing story and req reporting steps. - Iterates with `actions.forEach`, calling respective reporting functions only for missing annotations.
Tests linked to this story: - File: tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts - Header JSDoc: - `Tests for: docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md, docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md` - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION`, `@req REQ-ERROR-SPECIFIC`, `@req REQ-ERROR-CONSISTENCY`, `@req REQ-ERROR-SUGGESTION`. - Uses `RuleTester` with `ecmaVersion: 2020`. - Valid test cases: - Switch-case with comments immediately before `case 'z':` including `@story` and `@req`. - If-statement with preceding line comments containing `@story` and `@req`. - For loop, while loop, do-while loop, for-of, for-in, try/finally, try/catch, and switch case(s) all with proper annotations (both line and block comment forms). - Custom `branchTypes` configurations showing that unlisted branch types are ignored, and that only listed ones are enforced. - Invalid test cases: - If-statement lacking annotations: - Code: `if (condition) {}`. - Expected output: inserts `// @story .story.md` above `if`, and reports two errors with `messageId: "missingAnnotation"` and data `{ missing: "@story" }` and `{ missing: "@req" }`. - For loop with only `@story` present: - Expected output adds `// @req ` above the loop. - While loop with only `@req` present: - Expected output adds `// @story .story.md`. - Switch-case missing annotations, including variants with blank lines before the `case`: - Verifies `gatherBranchCommentText`’s ability to detect comments separated by one or two blank lines. - Do-while loop, for-of loop, for-in loop without annotations, each expecting inserted `@story` (and in some cases `@req`) and multiple `missingAnnotation` errors. - Try/catch blocks without annotations; tests expect four errors (two branches × two missing annotations) and an inserted `@story` before the try block. - Configurable scope invalid case: - Options: `{ branchTypes: ["UnknownType"] }`. - Expects errors that match `/should be equal to one of the allowed values/`, confirming invalid config behavior. - File: tests/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.test.ts - Header JSDoc: - References `docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` and `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - Tests for `validateBranchTypes`: - No options → returns `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES` as an array. - Valid custom `branchTypes` → returns the provided array. - Invalid types `["UnknownType", "Foo"]` → - Returns a listener object with `Program` handler. - Calling `Program(fakeNode)` results in `context.report` being called once per invalid type with messages containing `Value "" should be equal to one of the allowed values:`.

traceability.notes: The story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented and integrated. There is a concrete ESLint rule (`require-branch-annotation`) that detects missing @story and @req annotations on a clearly defined set of significant branch types (if/else, switch cases, try/catch, and all main loop constructs). Helper utilities implement branch type configuration, association of comments to branches (including special handling for switch cases), and parsing/reporting of annotations with appropriate autofix behavior. Tests explicitly reference this story, cover valid and invalid patterns for all targeted branch types, validate configuration behaviors (including invalid branchTypes), and assert on clear, specific error messages. The rule is wired into the plugin’s dynamic loading and included as an error in both recommended and strict configs. Dedicated rule documentation exists with examples and configuration guidance. The relevant tests run successfully under the project’s Jest-based test runner. All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for this story are therefore satisfied.
